Hi Gina — thanks, and great questions. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with the SOW language and a short carve-out we normally use for enterprise deals.

1) Reconciliation cadence: We do quarterly reconciliation by default for hosted API committed tiers. We will provide a quarterly true-up report that shows committed vs actual tokens consumed.

2) Make-goods: If you underconsume relative to the quarterly committed amount, we offer two options (customer chooses at contract signature):
   a) Credit: apply an on-invoice credit equal to the make-good amount for that quarter, usable against future invoices for the next 4 quarters; OR
   b) Carry-forward: roll the unused tokens forward to the next quarter once (one-quarter carry-forward).

   The SOW will call out which approach you prefer. For larger multi-quarter prepay commitments we can also discuss an annual reconciliation and make-good schedule.

3) Overages: Overage usage during a quarter is billed at the published overage rate (per-token). We can also add an auto-billing cap or tiered overage discounts if you expect high burst variability. Overage invoices are issued monthly.

I've attached a pricing workbook with commit tiers and sample math. I'll draft suggested SOW text and share a redline.

Attachments: Redwood_PRICING_2026.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Let me know which make-good option you prefer and whether you want quarterly or annual reconciliation as the default in the contract.
